question: A conducting ring is dropped vertically with its plane horizontal into a region where a magnetic field is directed upward and increases downward. What is the direction of the magnetic force on the ring while entering the field? Give reason.

options.A: Downward, because the magnetic field is upward.
options.B: Upward, because the induced effect opposes the increasing upward magnetic flux and hence opposes the downward motion.
options.C: Downward, because the induced current reinforces the increasing upward flux.
options.D: Zero, because the ring has no motion relative to the magnetic field.
